The story uses subtext effectively throughout, which enriches the academic setting rather than feeling forced. On the surface, the story is about a botched building renovation, but the subtext offers a sharp cultural commentary on the state of the humanities in the modern corporate university. 

For example, the corporate jargon used by the administration—calling a disruptive demolition an "Envelope Intervention" or a catastrophic leak an "unforeseen meteorological synergy"—carries the subtext of institutional indifference and gaslighting. Similarly, when Julian abruptly abandons his fierce crusade against "institutional necropolitics" to quietly ask whether his $500 stipend covers Sony headphones, the subtext reveals how easily academic radicalism folds into exhausted compliance and consumer comfort. Finally, the physical crumbling of Moppett Hall mirrors the intellectual preoccupations of the faculty (such as Arthur teaching the "Aesthetics of Ruin" while tar oozes down his chalkboard), turning the decaying setting into a rich symbol of the marginalized, dilapidated state of their academic discipline.
